cases.note: GNU 9.7 tr reads octal as \NNN with no leading zero required, so \141 is 'a'. Escape parsing is backend-independent, so this runs on ram and disk only.
tr has no \xHH — that is echo's grammar. GNU 9.7 drops the backslash and keeps the letter, so the set is {x, 4, 1} and 'axb41' loses all three.
\0 names NUL. Python's reader used to be a regex over eight named escapes, so this silently deleted nothing.
\c stops output in echo -e but is an ordinary unknown escape in tr, so the set is {c}. TypeScript's reader used to break out of the scan here and delete nothing.
